data.description: Guess Z or X for each qubit, measure it, then prepare two copies of what you saw.

single_copy_pass.label: One counterfeit passes
single_copy_pass.note: exact model value: copy 1 alone, averaged over the uniform secret

counterfeit_success.label: Both counterfeits pass (exact)
counterfeit_success.note: success of ONE specific attack: a LOWER bound on worst-case counterfeiting, never an upper bound

counterfeit_success.label: Both counterfeits pass (Monte Carlo)
counterfeit_success.source: lane-C Kraus channel against the lane-B bank (qmint.protocols.wiesner)
counterfeit_success.note: 25/1000 fresh notes; success of ONE specific attack: a LOWER bound on worst-case counterfeiting, never an upper bound

theorem_bound.label: W1 theorem: no counterfeiter beats
theorem_bound.source: A. Molina, T. Vidick, J. Watrous. Optimal counterfeiting attacks and generalizations for Wiesner's quantum money. TQC 2012, LNCS 7582, 45-64. arXiv:1202.4010v1; MVW2012 Theorem 1; https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.4010
theorem_bound.note: ideal game W1 only: one note, two outputs, exact verifier, no oracle

hardware.label: Quantum hardware
hardware.note: not run: paid hardware submission is disabled in this build (lane J); no QPU number exists

attack_result.quantum_channel_description: Guess Z or X for each qubit, measure it, then prepare two copies of what you saw.
attack_result.verifier_rule: exact projective BB84 verifier on every position; both candidates must pass

assumptions: one genuine note; the counterfeiter returns two candidate notes; the bank verifies both in the secret bases
Monte Carlo draws a FRESH secret note per trial (never repeated shots of one note)
data.simulator_caveat: A simulator's state is classical data that can be copied freely; nothing here demonstrates physical no-cloning. Only the modelled quantum register is simulated.
